summary: Order placement 500s are caused by dep-5101, the order-service v2.14.0 deploy at 12:10:00Z that added MarginCheckValidator to the validation chain and removed legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(): the new margin path dereferences a null marginProfile at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, throwing an NPE that surfaces as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders for F&O orders only (H1, confidence 0.74). The change is the only order-placement-touching change in 24h, precedes onset by ~2 min, and the failure is an NPE raised at the exact class/line the deploy added on the exact order type it targeted. Scope is fully closed: the unrestricted error query returns exactly 426 ERRORs resolving into exactly two signatures summing to the total (224 NPE + 202 "marginProfile is null") with no residual, and no non-FNO or non-NPE 5xx signature exists. Competing hypotheses are positively contradicted by flat CPU/connection-pool metrics (rejecting saturation) and flat ledger-db/kafka metrics with flat peer services (rejecting shared-dependency and sampling-artifact explanations). One hop remains unproven by design — whether marginProfile is locally constructed as null rather than returned null by an unregistered margin/account client — and the decisive code/config artifacts do not exist (deployment artifact has no diff; config API is empty for order-service), but this does not change the ranking or the remediation, so confidence is capped at 0.8 with H1 clearly ahead.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.14.0 MarginCheckValidator regression throws NPE for F&O orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0, deployed 12:10Z, rollout complete 12:10:08Z) added a new MarginCheckValidator to the validation chain and removed the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(). Only the F&O flow populates/reaches the new margin path; the marginProfile consumed at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 is null and the new code dereferences it, throwing a NullPointerException that escapes the validation chain and surfaces as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders. The escalation is now firmly supported by timing (deploy precedes onset by ~2 min), code-site identity (NPE at the exact line the deploy added), and scope (ERROR set is 100% FNO with zero residual signature). The unresolved hop is *why* marginProfile is null — the evidence shows no downstream call/error context, no timeout/RPC/circuit-breaker precursor, and no log line naming a source (F25–F28), which is consistent with an in-process/local null but does not positively prove it.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z, adding MarginCheckValidator and removing legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); rollout complete 12:10:08Z
Only F&O orders reach the new MarginCheckValidator path (legacy margin validation removed), so only FNO order types can hit the new code
For F&O orders the marginProfile consumed at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 is null; the new validator dereferences it with no callee/remote frame present

The NPE propagates out of the validation chain as an application-level error and is returned as HTTP 500 ('order rejected with 500: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>')
order-service 5xx error_rate steps from ~0.17–0.32% to 17.95% at the 12:12Z bucket (~2 min post-deploy) and stays elevated ~17.7–19.6% through 13:59Z
Symptom scope is derivatives-only: exactly two error signatures summing to all 426 entries (224 FNO NPE + 202 'order rejected 500' NPE), zero residual, with an EQ-orderType probe returning 0

Neighbour services that share order-service's datastores/queue are flat at onset (ledger-db, kafka) and the only stepped peer is api-gateway, mechanically explained as upstream propagation of order-service 500s

assumptions: The null marginProfile originates from the newly introduced code path (locally constructed / never-populated in-process object) rather than from a downstream call — supported only by absence of call/trace context (F25–F28), not positively proven
The v2.14.0 code path was active before 12:12:31Z (only supported by the single 12:10:08Z 'rollout complete' line; per-pod granularity unavailable, F46)
No non-FNO rejection signature exists that lacks the 'orderType=' token and would evade the probes (mitigated by the 426-total two-signature closure, F32/F35)

ranked_hypotheses.title: marginProfile is supplied by an unlisted margin/account dependency returning null
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The marginProfile dereferenced by MarginCheckValidator is supplied by an in-process call to a margin/account provider that never logged an error and returns null/empty. Because no order path reaches the NPE without dep-5101, H2 is properly a code×dependency co-cause rather than a standalone alternative: the deploy introduced the exposure, a dependency (or an unregistered/misconfigured client binding) supplies the null. Decisive evidence is code/config-side (validator DI/constructor wiring, line-88 statement, presence of a registered margin/account runtime client) and was not obtainable in this round — the dependency graph returns no margin-*/account-* node or edge (F44), the config API is empty for order-service (F45), and the deployment artifact exposes no diff (F43).
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: margin-service / account-service (unlisted downstream, or unregistered client binding in order-service)

causal_chain.claim: MarginCheckValidator obtains marginProfile from a margin/account provider that is not registered in order-service's returned dependency graph and has no metric target
That provider degrades, returns null, or its client binding was left unconfigured by dep-5101, so marginProfile is null for F&O accounts
The new validator dereferences the null at line 88 and the NPE surfaces as HTTP 500
No telemetry confirms or refutes such a dependency: margin-service/account-service are not metric targets, no log line names the source of marginProfile, and no timeout/RPC-failure line exists

assumptions: A margin/account provider exists and is reachable at runtime despite absent from the known service list and dependency graph
That provider changed/failed at ~12:12Z with no deployment or config record (the sweep returned only 2 unrelated deployments and one unrelated config change)
The null value is returned from a remote call rather than constructed locally

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (ledger-db / kafka / redis-cache) degradation surfacing as 500s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component in order-service's graph (ledger-db, kafka, or redis-cache via pricing-engine) degraded and produced order-placement failures surfaced as 500s, with the derivatives skew coincidental. Largely closed this round: ledger-db is flat across onset in connections_active, disk_used_pct, slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms (F37); kafka under_replicated_partitions is identically 0 and cpu/throughput show no step (F38–F40); pricing-engine/exchange-gateway (the shared-cache paths) error rates are flat (F23–F24). The only residual gap is redis-cache, whose error_rate metric does not exist and whose substitute metrics were never queried (F41).

causal_chain.claim: A shared component (ledger-db IOPS throttling, kafka broker stall, or cache failure) degrades at ~12:12Z
order-service's dependency call through that shared component fails during order placement
The failure surfaces as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, derivatives orders coincidentally more visible

assumptions: A shared component failed without appearing in deployment or config-change telemetry
The 500 signature would appear as an internally thrown NPE rather than a datastore/broker error
The derivatives-only scope could arise from a shared fault selective by order type

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's derivatives skew is a ticket-sampling artifact; fault is generic
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 500 fault affects all order types and the 'mostly derivatives' observation is support-ticket sampling bias. Now strongly contradicted: the unrestricted ERROR query returns exactly 426 entries resolving into exactly two signatures that sum to the total with zero residual, both NPE margin-path; an EQ-orderType probe returns 0; and the sole 'orderType=' token carrier is the FNO pattern — so all orderType-bearing errors are FNO. Residual (non-blocking) risk: if non-FNO rejections were logged without the 'orderType=' token they would evade every probe, but no non-NPE 5xx existed to account for them.

causal_chain.claim: Generic order-placement failure occurs for all order types
Support tickets over-represent derivatives orders

assumptions: Non-FNO errors would carry a signature never observed in the returned data

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity/resource saturation in order-service (or a dependency)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU/memory/connection saturation in order-service or a dependency caused error responses independent of any change. Positively contradicted: order-service CPU (~39.5–40.7%, peak 43.44%) and DB connection pool (~13.8–14.3, max 15.24) in use were flat across the 12:12 onset; ledger-db and kafka component metrics are also flat (F37–F40); and the signature is a deterministic FNO-scoped NPE on one code path, not a load-dependent timeout/saturation error.

order-service errors on order placement

assumptions: Unobserved memory/latency metrics might have degraded
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted by flat CPU and DB connection-pool metrics across onset (F11) and flat ledger-db/kafka component metrics (F37–F40), plus a deterministic input-scoped (FNO-only) NPE signature rather than load-dependent timeouts or saturation errors (F9, F32, F35).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (notification-service email.batch_size) unrelated
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A config change caused the incident; the only candidate cfg-2101 (notification-service email.batch_size 200->250, 11:21Z) is the trigger. The config API is empty for order-service over the full day and for all services in the 11:45–13:59Z onset window, so cfg-2101 is the sole config change in 24h and is unrelated in service, timing and key.

facts.statement: Exactly two deployments occurred in the 24h window; the only one touching order placement is order-service v2.14.0 (dep-5101) at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z, summary 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders', changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' and 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()', status live with rolled_back_at null. The other is portfolio-service v4.2.1 (dep-5088) at 09:36:00Z.

The dominant and only 5xx error signature is a NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) with orderType=FNO, plus 'order rejected with 500: ... marginProfile is null for account <n>' — raised inside order-service's own validation code, not as a callee 5xx/gRPC error.

The unrestricted order-service ERROR query over 12:00-14:00Z returned total_matched=426, breaking down into exactly two signatures that sum to the total with zero residual: MarginCheckValidator NPE orderType=FNO = 224 (first 12:12:31Z) and 'order rejected with <n>: ... marginProfile is null for account <n>' = 202 (first 12:12:44Z).

A non-FNO probe (contains 'orderType=EQ') returned total_matched=0 and the sole carrier of the 'orderType=' token is the FNO pattern (224 matches), so all orderType-bearing errors in the window are FNO.

order-service CPU (~39.5-40.7%, peak 43.44%) and DB connection pool in use (~13.8-14.3, max 15.24) were flat across the 12:12Z onset with no step change, indicating no local CPU or connection-pool exhaustion.

ledger-db is flat across onset in connections_active, disk_used_pct, slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms, and kafka under_replicated_partitions is identically 0 with flat cpu_pct and messages_in_per_s, contradicting a shared datasource/broker degradation mechanism.

Peer services payment-service, settlement-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and exchange-gateway show no error_rate step change at onset; api-gateway steps at 12:11Z, consistent with propagation from its downstream order-service.

The only config change in the 24h window is notification-service email.batch_size 200->250 (cfg-2101) at 11:21Z, a different service ~51 min before onset; the config API returns count 0 for order-service over the full day and for all services in the 11:45-13:59Z onset window.

The NPE log lines carry no downstream call context — only the MarginCheckValidator.java:88 frame with orderType/orderId — and full-text searches over the window returned 0 matches for 'timeout' (WARN), 'local', and no INFO/WARN line attributing marginProfile to any service.
order-service's dependency graph at depth 2 contains no node or edge named margin-*/account-*; margin-service and account-service are not metric targets, and marginProfile is nowhere identified.
The deployment artifact for dep-5101 exposes no changed-file/diff/line content and no per-pod rollout fields; the only rollout signal is a single 'rollout complete' telemetry line at 12:10:08Z.

redis-cache has no error_rate metric (available: connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so its health at onset could not be assessed — a data-source limitation rather than a zero reading.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back or feature-disable dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0), restoring the previous version with legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); alternatively disable the new margin-check path for F&O orders via the order-service flag mechanism.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 is the only order-placement-affecting change in 24h, precedes onset by ~2 min, and its new MarginCheckValidator line is the exact site of the FNO-only NPE that produces all 426 errors; both possible null-source readings are fixed by reverting this single change. It is still live with rolled_back_at null.

recommended_actions.action: After rollback, confirm order-service 5xx error_rate returns to baseline (~0.17-0.32%), the MarginCheckValidator NPE signature drops to zero in logs, and api-gateway error_rate (which stepped at 12:11Z) returns to ~0.11-0.29%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The step changes in order-service 5xx (F7) and api-gateway error_rate (F19, mechanistically upstream of order-service) provide a clean, measurable verification signal that distinguishes this fault from a shared-component issue.

recommended_actions.action: After rollback restores service, fix the v2.14.0 regression: ensure marginProfile is null-safe at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 — either populate it in the F&O path before the margin check or guard the dereference (null-check plus explicit validation error) — and restore equivalent coverage previously provided by the removed OrderRules.validateMargin(). Then re-deploy under a canary.
recommended_actions.rationale: The NPE is a null dereference on the F&O-only margin path at the line the deploy added, while the legacy validator it replaced was removed (F9, F25, F1, F13); the fix must cover both the local-null and unregistered-client possibilities with an explicit guard plus test coverage for F&O ordering.

recommended_actions.action: Add F&O-specific integration/contract tests and a pre-prod smoke check for POST /v1/orders that exercises the margin validation path, so a null marginProfile is caught before production; add a per-code-path null-check/assertion in the validation chain.
recommended_actions.rationale: The regression passed all pre-deploy gates despite an unconditional null dereference on the F&O path; the failure was 100% FNO-scoped (F10, F33, F34) and reproducible in the old F&O flow, so an F&O-only test would have caught it.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the margin path: log the source and lifecycle of marginProfile (local construction vs remote/DI-supplied, with a trace/span id), and add a metric/alert for margin-path validation failures. This closes the unverified null-source hop permanently.
recommended_actions.rationale: No log line, trace frame or config artifact identifies where marginProfile originates (F25, F26, F27, F28, F45), which is the one unproven link in the causal chain; making the source observable prevents a repeat of this ambiguity and enables fast discrimination between a code defect and a dependency fault.

recommended_actions.action: Gate F&O-relevant deployments behind canary/gradual rollout with per-pod ready timestamps and automatic 5xx-based rollback; make deployment artifacts expose diffs or changed-file lists so post-incident code review is possible.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101's rollout granularity is undeterminable (only one 'all pods ready' line, F28, F46) and get_deployments exposes no diff (F43), which prevented reading the changed code during the incident; canary plus artifact detail would have limited blast radius and shortened diagnosis.

findings.statement: Timeline is consistent with an in-process regression rather than a downstream dependency change: NPEs start at 12:12:31Z (103 MarginCheckValidator NPEs, first_seen 12:12:31Z) immediately after the v2.14.0 rollout ready at 12:10:08Z, and there is no order-service log evidence of any failed/slow downstream invocation preceding them.
Unrestricted order-service ERROR query over 12:00-14:00Z returned total_matched=426 with counts ERROR=426, spanning 12:12:31Z to 13:58:50Z.

The full error set breaks down into exactly two signatures whose counts sum to the total: NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:<n>) orderType=FNO orderId=<n> = 224 (first 12:12:31Z) and 'order rejected with <n>: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>' = 202 (first 12:12:44Z); 224+202=426 leaves no residual signature.
A non-FNO orderType probe (contains "orderType=EQ") over 12:00-14:00Z returned total_matched=0, truncated=false — no non-FNO orderType appears in the order-service ERROR logs.

The sole carrier of the 'orderType=' token is the FNO NPE pattern: filtering contains="orderType=" returns total_matched=224, matching exactly the 224 count of the orderType=FNO MarginCheckValidator pattern — i.e. all orderType-bearing errors are FNO.

Both signature families are the same root NPE: the 202 'order rejected with 500' entries are NPEs ('java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>', e.g. account 99733 at 12:12:44Z), so the only 5xx signature in the window is the NPE margin path — no 502/504-type or other non-NPE 5xx was observed in the returned data.

findings.statement: EXPLICIT (metadata-level) ABSENCE of any registered runtime client, gRPC stub, or HTTP client in order-service v2.14.0 targeting a margin/account provider: order-service's returned dependency graph at depth 2 contains exactly the caller→callee edges order-service→ledger-db (db), order-service→pricing-engine (http), order-service→exchange-gateway (http), order-service→kafka (queue-produce), pricing-engine→market-data-service, pricing-engine→redis-cache, exchange-gateway→exchange-api. No node or edge named margin-*, account-*, margin-service or account-service appears. Caveat: this is the dependency graph artifact, not the code/DI artifact the task asked for.

The config/flag API is EMPTY, not merely sparse: get_config_changes for service=order-service over the full day 00:00–13:59Z returns count 0 with changes [], and for all services over the tight 11:45–13:59Z onset window also returns count 0. Therefore no order-service client/DI/connection configuration object (e.g. a margin/account client registration, DI binding, or datasource/profile key) exists in the config metadata to cite — Q2 cannot be answered from config artifacts and no config change precedes the 12:12Z onset.

dep-5101's rollout granularity is NOT determinable from the deployment artifact — it records exactly one deployment object with no rollout strategy, pod list, or per-pod ready timestamps: status 'live', rolled_back_at null, and the only rollout-time evidence anywhere is the single telemetry line 'rollout complete' at 12:10:08Z (F28). F28 therefore has no independent pod-by-pod corroboration, and there is no artifact showing canary stages or a gradual ramp. Cannot exclude all-at-once; cannot confirm gradual.

No post-mortem precedent covers the removed legacy validator or a null margin-profile path: search for 'OrderRules.validateMargin legacy validator removed null marginProfile F&O derivatives' returns count 0. The only order-service margin-adjacent precedent is HIST-115 (order-service connection-pool misconfiguration, symptoms 'connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted') — a config_change category whose signature (pool exhaustion) is contradicted here by the flat in-use pool (~13.8–14.3, F11). Leads only, not evidence of causation.

Inference on Q1/Q2-sourcing from available (telemetry-level, not code-level) artifacts: the dereference at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 has no callee/remote frame anywhere in any NPE sample, no downstream-error context, and the window contains no timeout/RPC-failure/empty-response/'local' log line — while the returned dependency set has no margin/account client at all. This is consistent with line 88 dereferencing a value produced in-process (a builder/request-initialized or DI-supplied object) rather than the return value of a call to a registered margin/account provider, i.e. it does NOT support H2 (an unlisted margin dependency returning null). However, because the changed-file/diff and DI/connection config artifacts are absent (findings 1 and 3), the actual initialization of marginProfile cannot be positively established: an unregistered/unconfigured margin client injected at runtime remains formally possible.
